verses.text: Absalom, David's son, had a beautiful sister named Tamar. After a time, Amnon loved her.
Amnon was so tormented that he made himself ill because of his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin.
But Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother, who was a very crafty man.
Jonadab asked him, 'Why are you so haggard morning after morning?' Amnon said, 'I love Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.'
Jonadab suggested he lie down and pretend to be ill, then ask his father to send Tamar to prepare food for him.
Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came, Amnon asked him to let Tamar come make cakes in his sight.
David sent word to Tamar to go to her brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him.
Tamar went to Amnon's house and took dough, kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight and baked them.
She took the pan and emptied it before him, but he refused to eat and asked everyone to leave.
Amnon told Tamar to bring the food into the chamber so he could eat from her hand.
When she brought the cakes near him, he took hold of her and said, 'Come, lie with me, my sister.'
She answered, 'No, my brother, do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel.'
Tamar pleaded with him to speak to the king, who would not withhold her from him.
But he would not listen, and being stronger than she, he violated her and lay with her.
Then Amnon hated her with very great hatred, greater than the love with which he had loved her.
She said to him, 'No, my brother, for this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other that you did to me.'
He called his young servant and said, 'Put this woman out of my presence and bolt the door after her.'
Now she was wearing a long robe with sleeves, as the virgin daughters of the king were dressed.
Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long robe she wore, laid her hand on her head, and went away crying.
Her brother Absalom said to her, 'Has Amnon your brother been with you? Hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother.'
When King David heard of all these things, he was very angry.
But Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar.
After two full years Absalom had sheepshearers at Baal-hazor, near Ephraim, and invited all the king's sons.
Absalom came to the king and said, 'Behold, your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant.'
The king said, 'No, my son, let us not all go, lest we be burdensome to you.'
Then Absalom said, 'If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us.' The king asked, 'Why should he go with you?'
But Absalom pressed him until he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.
Absalom commanded his servants to mark when Amnon's heart was merry with wine and to strike him when commanded.
The servants of Absalom did to Amnon as commanded. Then all the king's sons arose and fled on their mules.
While they were on the way, news came to David, 'Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one is left.'
The king arose, tore his garments, and lay on the land. All his servants tore their garments.
Jonadab the son of Shimeah said, 'Let not my master suppose they have killed all the young men, for Amnon alone is dead.'
Jonadab advised David not to take it to heart as if all the king's sons were dead, for Amnon alone is dead.
But Absalom fled. The young man who kept watch lifted his eyes and saw many people coming from the road behind him.
Jonadab said to the king, 'Behold, the king's sons have come; as your servant said, so it has come about.'
As soon as he finished speaking, the king's sons came and lifted up their voice and wept, and the king also wept very bitterly.
But Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son day after day.
So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
And the spirit of the king longed to go out to Absalom, because he was comforted about Amnon, since he was dead.
